title: Recovering Causal Effects in Labeled Missingness Graphs with Context-Specific Mechanisms
banked_reason: D0.5 achieved subfield below the flagship floor: frozen delayed collider selection breaks the required CADMG Markov invariant, so the graphwise colored-hedge completeness promise cannot be delivered without a new architecture.
gap_reasons: The first missing flagship invariant is preservation of Inv(kappa) under delayed context selection. Without it, neither full legal-order confluence, the first-failure colored-district theorem, nor strictly positive realization of every colored hedge can be derived.
The frozen context-selection rule is not closed under the needed CADMG Markov invariant. A selection-aware graph formalism would be a new research architecture.
The baseline is not a graphwise completeness theorem and does not return a colored hedge.

The current persisted paper still has these unrepaired local findings: cited-hypothesis-missing@lem:colored-adjacent-swap; licensed-trace-not-derived@prop:figure3b-fix-select; closest_work_omitted@thm:two-comparator-strict-extension; ballast def:binary-response-handle and thm:binary-witness-observed-support-obstruction.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved a sound pointwise response-function/CAD decision theorem on the finite, strictly full-positive regular-maximal subclass, including direct score-contrast constancy and exact-free positive same-observed countermodels on negative cells. The bounded flagship lift to a graphwise colored recursion failed because delayed collider selection destroys the CADMG Markov invariant required for confluence and colored-hedge extraction; repairing that requires a new selection-aware graph architecture. The banked paper retains the listed local review findings and is not review-clean.
tldr: Finite labeled-missingness graphs encode context-specific mechanism deletions, but restricting to a missingness context too early can discard an identifying pre-restriction kernel. The procedure \(\operatorname{TCF}(\mathcal G,A,Y,P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) first constructs finite semialgebraic coordinate and direct score-contrast partitions from an edge-factorized response-function presentation, and then annotates fixed cells only with trace expressions verified on the whole cell. A coordinate or the declared score-coded NATE is recovered exactly when it is constant on the finite positive observational fiber; otherwise the corresponding negative cell yields two strictly positive same-observed lm-SCMs with different query values. Exact input is needed only to represent such witnesses, after which a finite diagnostic returns either a checked first-divergence record or an exhaustion tag, not a colored hedge. Figure 3(b) supplies the fix-then-select witness. On the common finite positive class, TCF preserves the de Aguas Proposition 4 and Mokhtarian root-control functionals, strictly extends the former on the endogenous-indicator proxy front-door family, and treats the latter as an embedding whose root premise is inapplicable to that family.
gap: De Aguas et al. give a sufficient weighted-adjustment criterion and the Figure 3(b) fix-before-select recovery; Mokhtarian et al. give completeness only for observed root controls. CSI search, missing-data recursion, and ordinary hedges do not jointly preserve label licenses, proxy traces, strict positivity, and the individual-edge semi-Markovian factorization.
fill: The proposal supplies that colored kernel, a two-way edge-factorized response-function equivalence, a symbolic semialgebraic partition theorem with an exact-input specialization contract, a concrete finite CAD bound, soundness, and an independent first-divergence compiler establishing colored-hedge completeness. It preserves both published comparator functionals and proves strict containment through the explicit delayed-selection functional on \(\mathcal G_\star\) and its parameterized EIPFD family.
